issues.issue: "The Client" is identified only as the law firm Jernigan, Copeland & Anderson, PLLC, leaving open whether the firm contracts on its own account or on behalf of the underlying tobacco-settlement litigation client whose cause the Scope of Services serves. The recital's descriptor "headquartered In Ridgeland, Mississippi" adds no entity limitation.

"Design of a full campaign plan" fixes no content, form, deadline or completion standard for the plan, so what performance discharges the item is undefined. The preamble's assertion that the scope "clearly defines" the services does not supply the missing measure.

The deliverables are introduced by "Including," an open-ended catch-all sitting in front of an enumerated list of documents, so it is unclear whether the listed items exhaust the Narrative & Messaging obligation or merely illustrate it. Nothing states how many of each, or to what standard, must be produced.

"produce all branding, digital and other needed collateral materials" pairs specific categories with the boundless catch-all "other needed," with no one identified to decide what is "needed." The scope of the production obligation therefore has no ascertainable outer limit.

This item makes all third-party research billable only "after cllent approval," while section 4.2's third-party expense paragraph requires prior Client approval only for Third-party Expenses of $1,000 or more. The two approval regimes cannot both govern research costs under $1,000.

"Undertake education activities to Inform them about the law suit" and a "natlonal list" of interested reporters set no size, frequency or content standard, so performance cannot be measured. "[R]eporters and news sources who are Interested In the tobacco settlement Issue" is itself an unbounded class.

"[B]est efforts" to place a national "breakout" story is undefined and the provision supplies no benchmark against which the effort is to be judged, while expressly disclaiming any guaranteed result. Whether any placement at all is required is therefore contestable.

This item promises to "write and place op-ed columns In key publications," an apparently result-based obligation, while the Earned Media item immediately above states that "the placement of stories Is not guaranteed" and reduces the duty to best efforts. Which standard governs op-ed placement cannot be settled from either provision alone.

"Perform outreach as necessary to groups IIkely to support the Client's efforts" leaves both the trigger ("as necessary") and the class of targets undefined, with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce given only as an example. Nothing states who judges necessity or likelihood of support.

"[B]uild a relevant audience with Interest In the Issues" sets no metric — no follower count, engagement level or posting cadence — by which the obligation could be tested. "[O]ne or more platforms" likewise leaves the commitment at its minimum.

"[P]erlodic monitoring" fixes no interval and "rapid response" no response time, so the frequency and speed of the required performance are indeterminate. The second sentence further conditions rapid response tasks on client approval without saying how approval is sought or timed.

Training is owed only "as necessary and approved by the client," so the obligation is entirely contingent on an approval that neither party is obliged to give or seek. Whether Xenophon must offer such training absent a client request is unresolved.

"Other communications tasks as agreed upon by the client" is a catch-all within the retainer-covered Scope of Services, while section 1.2 charges hourly for services "that fall outside the boundarles of the Scope of Services." Whether newly agreed tasks fall inside the $30,000 retainer or are separately billable turns on which provision controls.

"Xenophon's then-currently hourly rates" refers to a rate schedule that appears nowhere in the Agreement and is fixed unilaterally by Xenophon, leaving the price of Additional Services open. The garbled phrase "then-currently hourly rates" also obscures the date at which rates are set.

The "boundarles of the Scope of Services" that trigger hourly billing cannot be drawn because section 1.1 closes with "Other Tasks — perform other communications tasks as agreed upon by the client." Read together, every additional task could be characterised as either retainer work or Additional Services.

The Period of Performance is stated to be "on-going" with no end date, term length or renewal mechanism, so the Agreement's duration is indefinite on its face. The clause is also mis-numbered 2.4 in an Article whose only other section is 2.2, obscuring whether a section 2.1 is missing.

Termination on "60-days written notice" does not say what becomes of the $30,000 monthly retainer in section 4.1 during or at the end of the notice period, or whether a partial month is prorated. Sections 2.2 and 4.1 must be read together to know what is owed on termination, and neither addresses it.

The staffing list is prefaced "will Include but is not limited to," so the named individuals are neither guaranteed nor exhaustive and no minimum staffing commitment can be derived. Nothing ties any named person to any level of time on the engagement.

"[S]imilarly quallfled staff member" states no criterion of comparison — seniority, experience or title — against which a substitute for the section 3.1 personnel could be tested. The Client has no stated right to object to a substitution.

The stipulated remedy of "damages equal to one year of the employee's gross salary" does not say whose salary figure (the hiring party's offer or the prior salary) or at what date it is measured, and may be attacked as an unenforceable penalty. "[C]onclusion of this Agreement" is also undefined against the open-ended term in section 2.4.

The clause combines a flat "monthly retainer of $30,000" with an obligation to "track all hours and supply full detail," leaving it ambiguous whether the retainer is a fixed fee or a draw against time actually worked. Nothing states what happens if recorded hours are worth more or less than $30,000.

"[S]ubject to a possible calendar year price Increase not to exceed 5%" specifies no trigger, no notice requirement and no party empowered to declare the increase. Whether any increase can be imposed at all, and how often, is left open.
